title: South Australian Railways metropolitan network, 30 June 1938, as drawn on the PP No. 47 'Enlargement showing railways near Adelaide'

source.document: Map Showing Lines of Railways in South Australia, 30 June 1938, P.P. No. 47
source.method: Read by eye from the repository derivatives, rotated and enlarged. Station order follows the dots and labels on the inset. No timetable was consulted.

caveats: This is infrastructure drawn in 1938. It is not proof that every station had a passenger stop on a given day in 1947-48.
Order is marked 'medium' where labels crowd together on the photograph. Those positions should be checked against a 1948 working timetable.

The Glenelg line had been converted to an electric tramway in 1929, so it is not on the railway inset. It is added as a separate tram edge (see 'extra_edges') because the project's GAB reading depends on it.

Station names are the names printed on the map. Two stations carry a second, commonly used name as an alias (North Terrace = Adelaide; Commercial Rd = Port Adelaide). Each alias gives that station an extra initial.

lines.label: Hills line (Melbourne main line, inset portion)

extra_edges.note: Victoria Square-Glenelg electric tramway (from 1929), with a short city walk from the railway station. Weight 8 was fixed before scoring as roughly the station-hop equivalent of the same distance on the Brighton line (Adelaide-Oaklands). Intermediate tram stops are not modelled.
